key_insight: Combining whole-slide histology images with clinical data outperformed both single-modality models in four of six remission-prediction scenarios, but the best fusion method varied by outcome and input.
clinical_relevance: Multimodal AI may support research into remission prediction in inflammatory bowel disease, but these results do not establish readiness for clinical use.
method: Generated slide embeddings using an attention-based aggregator over patch embeddings from a frozen foundation model.
Compared 15 fusion methods combining slide and per-visit clinical embeddings in a modular framework.
Measured image reliance as the drop in balanced accuracy when slide embeddings were removed.
evidence_signal: In a prospective cohort of newly diagnosed patients, the best fusion method achieved macro-F1 scores of 0.57–0.75 across STRIDE-II-aligned remission-prediction scenarios using baseline or follow-up inputs.
watch_item: Similar predictive accuracy masked substantially different reliance on histology, so accuracy alone may not adequately characterize model behavior.
paper_title: Multimodal Fusion Methods for Whole-Slide Images and Clinical Data in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
